test_title: RRB NTPC Graduate Level CBT-I Official Paper (Held On: 23 Jun, 2025 Shift 1)
subject: general
question: If at the same rate of interest, in 2 years, the simple interest is 40 and compound interest, compounded annually, is 42, then what is the principal (in)?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

**Rate of Interest (R)** = [2 × (CI − SI) ÷ SI] × 100

⇒ R = [2 × (42 − 40) ÷ 40] × 100 = (4 ÷ 40) × 100 = 10%

**Principal (P)** = (SI × 100) ÷ (R × T)

⇒ P = (40 × 100) ÷ (10 × 2) = 4000 ÷ 20 = 200

**∴ The correct answer is 200.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** Simple Interest (SI) = 40, Compound Interest (CI) = 42, Time (T) = 2 years.

**Formula Used:** SI = (P × R × T) ÷ 100; CI − SI = Interest on first year SI.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/91e42381e13ad7449abc9401f5c095989b91467f02338d1b7369cb48761beccd.png] 

⇒ **Simple Interest** for 1 year = 40 ÷ 2 = 20

⇒ Difference (CI − SI) = 42 − 40 = 2

⇒ This difference 2 is the **interest** earned on the first year SI (20).

⇒ Rate of Interest (R) = (2 ÷ 20) × 100 = 10%

⇒ Since SI for 1 year is 20: 20 = (P × 10 × 1) ÷ 100

⇒ 20 = P ÷ 10

⇒ P = 20 × 10 = 200

**∴ The correct answer is 200.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Difference between CI and SI for 2 years

The difference (D) is calculated as D = P(R/100)².

Relation for 2 years

The ratio of CI to SI for 2 years is CI/SI = (200 + R) / 200.

Difference between CI and SI for 3 years

The difference is calculated as D = P(R/100)² × (3 + R/100).</p
